context: A teacher walks a uni student through a philosophy paper
purpose: Teach: 落下/最高裁判所/拒絶/探求/力学/神学/高層/個体

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、神学と力学の歴史的対立を扱うんですね。
lines.en: Your paper addresses the historical tension between theology and mechanics—interesting combination.
lines.style: Warm, genuine interest. Leans forward slightly. Steady eye contact. Opening on the subject draws him in, not from above. Unhurried pacing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。物体の落下に関する論争、最高裁判所のような決着点はない、と論じます。
lines.en: Yes. I'm arguing that debates over falling objects never reached a definitive resolution—not like a final court ruling.
lines.style: Careful articulation, slightly rushed underneath. Searching for the right frame. Earnest but uncertain if the analogy lands. Faint self-consciousness on the comparison.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 高層建築の発展も、それぞれの探求が支えになった。
lines.en: And the rise of tall buildings grew out of both traditions pushing each other forward.
lines.style: Gentle realization dawning. Speaking as though connecting dots aloud for him. Warm, not instructional. Measured tempo, giving space for thought.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 宗教側からの拒絶反応、章を割いて分析します。
lines.en: I've dedicated a whole chapter to mapping out the resistance from religious scholars—their actual arguments, not caricatures.
lines.style: Quick, firm. Small pride in the rigor. Eyes brighten slightly when naming the focus. Matter-of-fact but carries weight, like he's quietly defending his own work.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 観察対象の個体、データの扱いも丁寧に。
lines.en: Make sure your treatment of individual specimens and data sources stays as careful as your arguments.
lines.style: Shifts slightly more formal, but still warm. Not a warning—a gift of foresight. Specific and practical. Delivered with quiet confidence that he'll listen.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Nod implicit in the voice. Genuine gratitude, not just polite acknowledgment. Quiet, steady. Settles into the feedback.
